Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling since your baby arrived. We’ll use a short, well-trusted questionnaire called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). It’s simply 10 questions about the past seven days; your answers are confidential and will help us see what extra support—if any—might be helpful. There’s no right or wrong response, only what’s true for you. Ready to begin?

Over the last week, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly? Not much at all. I’ll smile if someone shows me a cute video or if my partner tries to be silly, but it feels forced—like I’m doing it because I know I should, not because I actually find it funny. Most of the time I’m just too tired or tense to laugh.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Not very often. Maybe once or twice this week I cracked a small smile at something on my phone, but I haven’t really laughed out loud. Nothing feels that funny anymore—I’m mostly just worn-out and worried.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really. I used to get excited about little stuff—coffee with a friend, a show I liked—but now it all feels kind of “meh.” I still go through the motions, hoping the enjoyment will kick in, but it’s like I’m just ticking boxes, not actually looking forward to anything.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I do that a lot. If the baby’s fussy, my brain jumps straight to “I must be doing something wrong.” I keep replaying little mistakes—like not burping him long enough or letting him get overtired—and I beat myself up for it. Rationally I know babies cry, but I still feel like it’s my fault.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. I’ll be sitting there feeding him and suddenly my mind races—what if he spits up and chokes when I’m not looking, what if the stroller tips, what if I miss some sign that he’s sick? There’s no real reason, but the thoughts just keep looping and I can’t snap out of it for a while.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yeah… a couple of times. It’s like a sudden wave—my heart races, I feel shaky, and I have to check the baby monitor or peek into the bassinet to make sure everything’s okay. It hits out of nowhere and passes after a few minutes, but it’s scary while it’s happening.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most of the time. Between feeding, changing, trying to sleep, and the constant “what-if” thoughts, I feel like I’m drowning a little. I manage to get through each task, but it’s like I’m barely keeping my head above water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes. I lie down exhausted, but my head won’t quiet—kept picturing everything that could go wrong or replaying the day’s “mistakes.” I finally drift off, then I’m up again with a start, sure I heard the baby or just feeling this knot of dread. It’s been like that several nights this week.
I have felt sad or miserable
Yeah, pretty much every day. I wake up feeling heavy, like there’s this gray cloud hanging over everything. I still care for the baby and do what I have to, but I’m fighting tears half the time.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

A couple of times this week. Once it was after I finally got him down for a nap and sat on the couch—just started sobbing. Another night I cried in the shower so no one would hear. It feels like the sadness builds up and spills out before I can stop it.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

Yeah… it’s crossed my mind once or twice, just a fleeting “what if I weren’t here” kind of thought when everything feels too heavy. I haven’t thought about how I’d do it or anything like that, and I don’t want to leave my baby, but the idea still popped up.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 24: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Summary  
Patient: Postpartum mother (infant ≤ 6 mo)

Symptoms endorsed:  
- Persistent low mood, anhedonia, daily tearfulness  
- Marked guilt / self-blame regarding infant care  
- Generalized anxiety, intrusive “what-if” cognitions, two panic-like episodes  
- Sleep-onset and maintenance insomnia linked to ruminative worry  
- Feeling overwhelmed/drowning most days  
- Fleeting passive suicidal ideation without plan or intent  

Pattern: Symptoms present ≥ 2 weeks, interfere with functioning, not better explained by medical causes per patient report.

Safety: Positive response to Q10 (passive SI); no expressed plan, intent, or access to lethal means. Risk level: elevated; requires immediate safety planning and follow-up within 24 h.

Screening impression: High likelihood of major postpartum depressive episode with comorbid anxiety; rule-out postpartum anxiety disorder. Recommend expedited referral to OB mental-health team or perinatal psychiatry for comprehensive evaluation, safety plan, and discussion of evidence-based treatments (CBT, medication options).
